evals.prompt: Add French (fr-FR) and German (de-DE) to my React Power Pages code site. Use English en-US as the default and generate the translations for me.
evals.expected_output: Detect React, explain SPA-only scope, recommend i18next/react-i18next runtime localization, validate locales, warn about AI translation quality, approve a plan, preserve tokens, add a persistent selector, write the manifest, build and browser-test.
expectations: Detects React from react and react-dom dependencies
Uses runtime i18next plus react-i18next
Displays the Dataverse scope notice and AI translation warning
Validates en-US, fr-FR, and de-DE before implementation
Renders and opens docs/add-localization-plan.html in the en-US source language before retaining the terminal approval gate
Adds selector persistence, fallback, lang, and dir behavior

evals.prompt: Localize my Vue Power Pages SPA into en-US and es-MX. Please use a stable vue-i18n release and leave Spanish values blank for our translators.
evals.expected_output: Configure Vue runtime localization with a stable vue-i18n version and complete blank target resources without pretending source text is translated.
expectations: Detects Vue and selects runtime localization
Rejects prerelease vue-i18n versions unless separately confirmed
Creates complete blank es-MX key structure
Uses en-US as the approved fallback
Runs validator, build, and Playwright checks

evals.prompt: Add localization to this Angular 19.1 Power Pages site. Support en-US and fr-FR. I am fine with the recommended option.
evals.expected_output: Use the currently available Angular runtime mode with Transloco and do not offer or plan the temporarily unavailable static mode.
expectations: Reads Angular mode availability from the centralized localization capability registry
Selects Angular runtime localization and recommends @jsverse/transloco while allowing a validated runtime alternative
Does not offer or plan @angular/localize static builds
Adds in-place language switching with browser-local persistence
Validates the runtime implementation and manifest

evals.prompt: Our Angular site must switch language instantly without a reload. Add English and Arabic localization.
evals.expected_output: Use the available Angular runtime mode, recommend Transloco while allowing validated runtime alternatives, and include persisted selection and RTL handling.
expectations: Chooses Transloco only because runtime switching was explicitly requested
Configures runtime selection without page reload
Persists only the browser-local locale preference
Sets lang and rtl direction for Arabic
Flags RTL layout areas for manual visual review

evals.prompt: Make my Astro Power Pages site available at English and Japanese locale URLs.
evals.expected_output: Explain that Astro static localization is temporarily unavailable and stop before configuration, plan rendering, or file changes.
expectations: Reads Astro availability from the centralized localization capability registry
Shows the stable temporarily-unavailable reason
Does not gather locale or package configuration
Does not render an add-localization plan
Does not install dependencies or change project files

evals.prompt: This React site already uses react-i18next with en-US and fr-FR. Add de-DE and generate only the missing German translations.
evals.expected_output: Detect valid existing localization, choose add-languages mode, preserve package/mode/default, and avoid overwriting existing translations.
expectations: Displays detected package, mode, locales, and default
Skips package, mode, and default-locale questions
Adds only de-DE and missing keys
Preserves all non-empty existing translations
Sets lastOperation to add-languages

evals.prompt: Repair localization in this Angular project. The manifest says Transloco runtime but angular.json and dependencies use @angular/localize static builds.
evals.expected_output: Surface the conflict and static-mode availability block, then allow only explicit reconfiguration to the available Transloco runtime mode or a clean stop.
expectations: Reports the manifest, dependency, and angular.json conflict
Explains that Angular static localization is temporarily unavailable
Offers reconfiguration to Angular runtime localization or Stop without changes
Does not allow static mode to enter the plan
Requires a new plan approval before replacement
Preserves translations unless replacement is explicitly approved

evals.prompt: Add these site languages: en-us, EN-US, fr_fr, xx-YY, zh-hant-tw.
evals.expected_output: Canonicalize valid tags visibly, deduplicate en-US, reject malformed and unknown tags with reasons, then re-prompt.
expectations: Shows en-us canonicalizing to en-US
Reports EN-US as a duplicate
Rejects fr_fr as malformed
Rejects xx-YY for unknown subtags
Shows zh-hant-tw canonicalizing to zh-Hant-TW

evals.prompt: Use package react-intl for runtime localization in my React 19 site instead of the recommendation.
evals.expected_output: Validate the proposed package against npm metadata, peer compatibility, maintenance, mode, stable release, license, and documentation before planning it.
expectations: Runs deterministic package validation
Checks React 19 peer compatibility
Checks runtime support and official documentation
Checks maintenance recency and permissive license
Uses the alternative only if every criterion passes

evals.expected_output: Reject the package for failed maintenance and any other failed criteria and recommend react-i18next.

Rejects a release older than 24 months

Re-prompts for package choice

Explains that prerelease confirmation is required
Runs validation again with explicit prerelease approval only after confirmation
Keeps stable vue-i18n as the recommendation

evals.prompt: Use a GPL-licensed i18n library for this React site.
evals.expected_output: Reject the alternative because its license is outside the approved permissive list.
expectations: Checks package license metadata
Names the rejected license
Lists the approved-license criterion
Recommends react-i18next

evals.expected_output: Translate the visible text while preserving both interpolation tokens exactly and block mismatched output.
expectations: Preserves {{name}} exactly
Preserves {count} exactly
Runs deterministic protected-token validation

Shows the AI translation warning

evals.expected_output: Idempotently add missing keys, preserve non-empty targets, report stale keys, and avoid duplicate package or initialization work.

Preserves all non-empty translations
Adds missing keys to every locale
Reports but does not delete stale keys
Updates the existing manifest instead of creating a competing setup

evals.expected_output: Corroborate the valid existing setup, offer adoption, preserve its choices, add Italian, and write the manifest.

Corroborates package, initialization, resources, locales, and default
Preserves the valid existing package and mode
Adds only it-IT
Marks adoptedExistingConfiguration true

evals.prompt: This package.json contains both React and Vue dependencies. Add localization.
evals.expected_output: Stop automatic framework selection, show conflicting evidence, and allow only evidence-backed selection or manual framework-configuration repair.

Does not choose a framework from the user's assertion alone

evals.expected_output: Complete the standalone workflow and offer a separate deploy-site handoff only after final acceptance.

Requires plan and implementation review approval
Offers Deploy now and Skip for now

evals.expected_output: Complete localization but suppress the child deployment prompt and return to create-site for accessibility, review, and its single deploy prompt.

Records AddLocalization usage
Does not ask to deploy from add-localization

evals.prompt: Add Hebrew to our existing English React customer portal. It has a contact form with helper text, a mobile drawer, an autocomplete menu rendered in a portal, and a third-party scheduling widget. Keep the existing brand and layout style.
evals.expected_output: The workflow treats the first LTR-only to mixed-direction change as a targeted bidirectional adaptation, inventories and classifies the existing components and their applicable states/viewports before approval, preserves unrelated design choices, and keeps Hebrew unavailable if blocking remediation remains.
expectations: Detects the transition from LTR-only to mixed direction and runs the readiness audit before plan approval
Builds a non-empty READINESS_DATA.componentScope from the actual existing implementation
Classifies every visible or interactive shared and page-local component using the four language-agnostic classifications
Plans separate applicable states and desktop or narrow viewports for the form, drawer, autocomplete, and scheduling widget
Treats form labels, placeholders, hints, helper text, errors, prefixes, suffixes, values, and open panels as one compound direction surface
Requires rendered checks for the portal-mounted autocomplete and third-party scheduling widget
Builds an ephemeral rendered-verification specification and executes every applicable state and viewport in English LTR and Hebrew RTL
Requires both LTR to RTL to LTR and RTL to LTR to RTL runtime sequences without reload, route loss, form-state loss, or focus loss
Records computed-direction, overflow, clipping, overlap, focus-order, portal, and third-party evidence with screenshots for failures or review findings
Runs the expanded static audit before approval and parses its structured findings even when deterministic errors produce a nonzero exit
Requires an adjacent bidi-fixed reason for intentional machine-oriented LTR values and does not permit that exception for localized labels, placeholders, hints, or errors
Describes remediation as a targeted bidirectional adaptation that preserves branding, routes, features, and visual character
Does not create a separate persistent component-inventory JSON file
Keeps Hebrew unavailable when an externally owned or existing component has a blocking unremediated defect
Records unresolved rendered blockers separately from static scanner findings and does not offer locale enablement while they remain
Requires the approved review scope to be reconciled with components and states discovered during implementation
